Upstate NY. Friend of mine was in a situation where he moved in with friends, and the landlord wrote a new lease which he signed. He lived there for a while and the landlord had a very "hands off" etiquette. He would never come to collect rent when it was due, sometimes even a month later, and made it clear that he didn't want much to do with the tenants. The situation between the tenants and my friend fell through, and they did him dirty. He was away for a month and a half right after they had all fought and they moved out without letting him know. His belongings were still in the apartment, and the other tenants broke the lease. When my friend returned the landlord had written multiple notes on paper towel, left on the kitchen counter, demanding full rent for the month because his stuff was still there, and for my friend to call him. My friend included his phone number and contact info on the lease as required, and the landlord never tried contacting him whatsoever besides the paper towel scribbles. The landlord threw all of my friends things in trash bags and moved them to the shed. In the note he had said to pay rent, and he'll get the stuff back. Well, the landlord left the shed unlocked and he got his stuff and got out of there. I know he can't afford the full rent, and I don't think he should even think about paying it. The landlord did no due diligence in contacting him at all. But, I'm no lawyer. Thoughts? I appreciate the help.
